### Measured, against exact

1000 replications per point; every axis pair in each box. Correlation and variance ratio Var(g(x) - g(y)) / (Var g(x) + Var g(y)): median (quartiles) over pairs; 1 is independent sampling, above 1 CRN is worse than independent. Largest |z|: the measured correlation against the exact one (0 without CRN), Fisher z over a jackknife standard error; every pair was required to be within 4.5. Normal-theory error: pairs where leaving one replication out gives a correlation of exactly 1, so the jackknife is undefined and 1 / sqrt(n - 3) is used instead.

### The solvers: quality at matched counted simulations

Runs: 360, Python ['3.14.8'], budget [20000], 20 seeds per configuration; the seeds of docs/bench_crn.py's runs. Quality: the Hausdorff distance between the true images of the returned set and of the efficient set; lower is better. Median, then seeds where CRN is better / same / worse than the default arm on the same seed. "-": no iteration finished by that checkpoint.
